families.custody: Railway migrator-only schema-owner URL and role-bootstrap passwords; derived application URL on the API; derived key-admin URL only in a protected ephemeral operator shell
families.rotation: Generate distinct environment-local application and key-admin passwords, deploy the migrator to reconcile fixed roles and exact ACLs, deploy the API with only the derived fmarch_application URL, and prove the exact commit. Use the derived fmarch_key_admin URL only in an ephemeral operator shell; after successful redeploy and connection drain, retire the prior passwords and URLs.
Set a new key and marker atomically on both services, deploy both, verify authenticated source attribution, then retire the prior value.

families.custody: Railway API service variables with operator escrow outside the repository
families.rotation: Add the prior KEK to the historical read ring, deploy a new active KEK and KID, then use fmarch-event-key-admin to plan, fence, and migrate every stream-DEK and registered direct envelope. Run the distinct removal rehearsal with the old KID absent; remove the hosted historical secret, redeploy every replica, and prove exact-commit startup/readiness before finalizing the immutable retired tombstone. Keep the old key only in offline escrow until every backup that can contain old-KID ciphertext has expired or been rotation-rehearsed on restore.

families.custody: Independent archive escrow outside the runtime database and repository
families.rotation: Stage and deploy the new archive KEK and KID with the prior archive KEK retained for reads, prove old archive import and new archive export, then retire the prior KEK only after the declared archive-retention window.

families.custody: Railway API service variable with operator escrow outside the repository
families.rotation: Follow docs/ops/profile-handle-index-rotation.md exactly. In a protected one-shot shell, provide the active key/KID plus FMARCH_PROFILE_HANDLE_INDEX_REPLACEMENT_KEY and run fmarch-profile-index-admin profile-handle-index plan with explicit current/replacement KIDs. Drain every API/profile writer (including pre-lease binaries), then run reindex with --writers-drained --execute. While traffic remains drained, atomically set the API service's active key and KID to the replacement values, remove the replacement-only variable, deploy, and require startup audit/readiness plus duplicate-handle proof. Only after that successful redeploy, retire the prior key from every live service variable; retain it solely in offline escrow through the declared recovery window, then destroy the escrowed copy and record the retired KID in the release record. Never flip the API secret first or retain derived tokens in canonical profile events.
Issue environment-local bucket credentials, update the API references and marker, deploy and prove object reads/writes, then revoke the prior credentials.

families.custody: Dedicated environment-local Railway Bucket plus client-side wrapping and journal-authentication secrets
families.rotation: Provision and explicitly bootstrap a new dedicated authority, migrate only active wrapped keys plus every authenticated revocation, atomically update genesis/revision and both KIDs/keys, deploy and verify startup reconciliation/readiness, then revoke prior bucket credentials and retire prior client-side keys without ever restoring a deleted subject key.

families.custody: WorkOS environment plus Railway frontend service variables
families.rotation: Rotate the environment-local API key and cookie password, deploy the frontend and API marker together, verify login/callback/session exchange, then revoke the prior API key; cookie-password rotation intentionally invalidates unfinished ceremonies.
